evidence_kind: Declared software common-lock ownership contract; no hardware law or measurement
source_basis: JUCE UndoManager is not a concurrent container: worker APVTS replaceState clears it while toolbar reads and user transaction creation previously bypassed the plugin common tree lock.
Every snapshot/restore and complete undo/redo mutation already owns the same common tree lock; history reads and opening a transaction must join that exclusion mechanism.

fixtures.name: toolbar_history_snapshot_reads_own_common_lock
fixtures.sequence: Read canUndo, canRedo, undo description and redo description as a detached history snapshot. All four production toolbar query callbacks must consume this synchronized snapshot instead of a raw UndoManager reference. A private reader witness, invoked inside the actual production read scope and reading the same real UndoManager fields, uses another thread's nonblocking tryEnter; acquisition must fail. After a real user edit, undo and redo, compare the snapshot fields exactly with the corresponding history state under the common lock.
fixtures.implementation_constraint: Use the production read scope; no duplicate reference lock, sleep inference, or runtime mode switch.

fixtures.name: user_transaction_open_owns_common_lock
fixtures.sequence: Open a named user transaction through the actual production transaction-open scope, with a private transaction-writer witness wrapping the real UndoManager::beginNewTransaction call. A separate thread's nonblocking tryEnter on the common tree lock must fail at that call. Verify the real transaction name after creation. Existing user gesture coalescing and history tests remain unchanged.
fixtures.implementation_constraint: The common lock covers synchronization and opening the transaction in one scope. Worker snapshot/restore and transaction creation cannot overlap their live history accesses. No MessageManagerLock or synchronous message dispatch is allowed.

required_mutation_checks: Remove the common lock from the production history snapshot reader: its actual-reader lock witness must fail.
Remove the common lock from the production transaction-open scope: its actual transaction writer witness must fail.
preservation: Keep the original six fixtures and seven mutations unchanged.
Keep both recording-ownership/value-preservation fixtures and their two mutations unchanged.
Keep every existing UI, undo, automation, serialization, Pure/default, native host, parameter identity and audio compatibility requirement unchanged.
Timeouts, deadlocks, compilation failures, crashes and environmental harness errors do not qualify a mutation.
